x: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Commentary on the sura "By the heaven and the Night-Comer (al-Ṭāriq)"
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

By the heaven and the Night-Comer (1) And what will make you know what the Night-Comer is? (2) The piercing star (3) Every soul has a guardian over it (4) So let man consider from what he was created (5) He was created from a gushing fluid (6) Emerging from between the backbone and the tarāʾib (7) Indeed He is able to bring him back (ʿalā rajʿihī) (8) On the Day when secrets are put to the test (9) Then he will have no power and no helper (10)

Our Lord, majestic is His praise, swears by the heaven and by the Night-Comer (al-ṭāriq), which is among the shining stars: it comes at night and is hidden by day. Everything that comes at night has "knocked" (ṭaraqa). The commentators spoke in line with what we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās:
m: By the heaven and the Night-Comer
. He said: The heaven and what knocks (yaṭruqu) in it

c: Bishr related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatāda:
m: By the heaven and the Night-Comer (1) And what will make you know what the Night-Comer is?
. He said: A night-comer that comes at night

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda,
m: . He said: The appearance of the stars. He says: it knocks at you by night

c: I was told on the authority of al-Ḥusayn,
m: who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His saying:
And what will make you know what the Night-Comer is?

The Exalted says to His Prophet Muḥammad, God bless him and grant him peace: What has made you aware, Muḥammad, of what the Night-Comer is, by which I swore? Then He, majestic is His praise, explained it, saying: it is the piercing star (al-najm al-thāqib), meaning that its light blazes and glows. The commentators spoke in line with what we have said.

Muḥammad b. Saʿd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās:
m: . He said: These are the shining stars, and their "piercing" (thuqūb) is when they give light.

c: Ibn Ḥumayd related to us, saying: Yaḥyā b. Wāḍiḥ related to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn related to us, from Yazīd, from ʿIkrima
m: . He said: The one that pierces (yanqubu).

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, saying: ʿĪsā related to us, and al-Ḥārith related to me, saying: al-Ḥasan related to us, saying: Warqāʾ related to us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding God's saying
. He said: The one that glows

c: Bishr related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatāda:
Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda:
Yūnus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said
m: . He said: The Arabs used to call the Pleiades (al-Thurayyā) "the star" (al-najm), and it is said that the piercing star is the one called Saturn (Zuḥal). "Piercing" (thāqib) also means the one that has risen above the stars; and the Arabs say of a bird, when it reaches the belly of the sky in height: "it has pierced" (thaqaba). And the Arabs say: "Athqib nārak," that is, make your fire give light

x: And His saying:
h
Every soul has a guardian over it
. The reciters differed in the reading of this. Abū Jaʿfar, among the reciters of Medina, and Ḥamza, among the reciters of Kufa, read
h
lammā ʿalayhā
with a doubled mīm
n
. It is also reported that al-Ḥasan read it that way
n

c: Aḥmad b. Yūsuf related to me, saying: Abū ʿUbayd related to us, saying: Ḥajjāj related to us, from Hārūn,
m: that al-Ḥasan used to read it
in kullu nafsin lammā ʿalayhā ḥāfiẓ

with the doubled mīm, and he would say: "except that over it is a guardian." And so it is for every occurrence in the Qurʾān, with the heavy form (bi-l-tathqīl). Among the people of Medina Nāfiʿ, and among the people of Basra Abū ʿAmr, read (lamā) with the light form

, meaning: "in kullu nafsin la-ʿalayhā ḥāfiẓ," with the lām as the answer to "in" and the "mā" after it as a redundant particle (ṣila). That being so, there is no doubling in it. The reading that I prefer above any other here is the light one
, because that is the usage known from the speech of the Arabs, and a group of those knowledgeable about Arab speech have rejected that the doubled form is known in Arab usage. Yet al-Farrāʾ

used to say: "We do not know the basis for the doubled form here, and we think it is a dialect of Hudhayl, who make "illā" with the lightened "in" into "lammā" and go no further than that, as if he had said: "No soul but has a guardian over it."" If what al-Farrāʾ mentioned, that it is the dialect of Hudhayl, is sound, then reading it that way is permissible and correct, although, if that is established in our view, the preferred reading is still the other one, the light form, because that is the one known from Arab speech, and one should not abandon the better known for the less known.

c: Aḥmad b. Yūsuf related to me, saying: Abū ʿUbayd related to us, saying: Muʿādh related to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, who said:
m: in kullu nafsin lammā ʿalayhā ḥāfiẓ

, and he rejected it and said: "Glory be to God! Glory be to God!" So the meaning of the verse is: every soul has a guardian from its Lord, who guards its deeds and records against it whatever it earns of good or evil. The commentators spoke in line with what we have said.

m: Every soul has a guardian over it

c: Bishr related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatāda
m: Every soul has a guardian over it

x: And His saying:
h
So let man consider from what he was created
. The Exalted says: Let the human being who denies the resurrection after death, and who rejects God's power to give him life after his death, consider
h
from what he was created
. He says: from what thing his Lord created him. Then He, majestic is His praise, informed us of what He created him from, saying:
h
He was created from a gushing fluid

, meaning from a poured fluid (māʾ madfūq). It is among the expressions the Arabs formed on the pattern fāʿil while the sense is mafʿūl, and it is said that those among the Arab tribes who use this most are the inhabitants of the Hijaz, when it is in the manner of an adjective, [as in their saying: this is]
n
sirrun kātim (a "concealing" secret, meaning a concealed one) and hammun nāṣib (a "wearying" worry, meaning a wearisome one), and the like.
And His saying:

Emerging from between the backbone and the tarāʾib
. He says: it comes out from [the backbone of the man and the tarāʾib of the woman. It is also said that it comes out from]
n

between that. The meaning of the statement is: from both of them, as one says: "Much good will come out from between these two things," meaning: it will come out from both. The commentators differed over the meaning of "the tarāʾib" and its location.

On the Day when secrets are put to the test

with a report among the reports of the Resurrection indicates that what precedes it also belongs to the same subject, as does

On the Day when secrets are put to the test

He means: the Day when the inner secrets of the servants are tried, and there appears from them on that day what was hidden in the world from the eyes of people, of the obligations that God had imposed on him and charged him to perform. The commentators spoke in line with what we have said.

m: . He said: This one splits open from what is beneath it. Abū Rajāʾ said: ʿIkrima was asked about it, and he said: This one splits open for provision

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, saying: ʿĪsā related to us, and al-Ḥārith related to me, saying: al-Ḥasan related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid:
Al-Ḥārith related to me, saying: al-Ḥasan related to us, saying: Warqāʾ related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid:
m: . He said: The splitting is like the maʾzim, other than the valleys and other than the washed-out banks (jurf)

c: Bishr related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatāda
m: : it splits open for the fruits and for plants, as you have seen

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda:
m: . He said: It splits open for plants (4).

c: Yūnus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said
m: Then We split the earth, splitting (26) And caused grain to grow in it (27) And grapes and fresh fodder
[ʿAbasa: 26–28], to the end of the verse. He said: He split it for tillage

c: I was told on the authority of al-Ḥusayn,
m: who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His saying

x: And His saying:
h
Indeed, it is a decisive word
. The Exalted says: This statement and this report is
h
a decisive word
. He says: a word that separates truth from falsehood by its clear exposition. The commentators spoke in line with what we have said, though differing in how they expressed it.
Some of them said: a true word.
Some of them said: a word of judgment (ḥukm).
Mention of those who said this:

c: ʿAlī related to me, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us, saying: Muʿāwiya related to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās
m: Indeed, it is a decisive word

c: Bishr related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatāda
m: Indeed, it is a decisive word

x: And His saying:
h
And it is not amusement
. He says: it is not play and not falsehood. The commentators spoke in line with what we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: ʿAlī related to me, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us, saying: Muʿāwiya related to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās
Muḥammad b. ʿAmr related to me, saying:
m: related to us, saying: ʿĪsā related to us, and al-Ḥārith related to me, saying: al-Ḥasan related to us, saying: Warqāʾ related to us, both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding His saying

x: And His saying:
h
Indeed, they plot a plot
. The Exalted says: Those who deny God and His Messenger, and the promise and the warning, are scheming a scheme.
And His saying:
h
And I plot a plot
. He says: and I scheme a scheme. His scheming against them, majestic is His praise, is His granting them respite in their disobedience and their disbelief in Him.
And His saying:
h
So give the disbelievers time
. The Exalted says to His Prophet Muḥammad, God bless him and grant him peace: So give the disbelievers time, Muḥammad, and do not hasten against them,
h
give them time, a little
. He says: give them respite for a short while, and wait for them until the appointed time, which is the time when retribution falls upon them. The commentators spoke in line with what we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

m: ʿAlī related to me, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us, saying: Muʿāwiya related to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās

x: regarding His saying:
h
give them time, a little
. He says: a short while
n

c: Bishr related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatāda:
Yūnus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said
m: So give the disbelievers time; give them time, a little

. He said: Give them time, and do not hasten against them. He left them, until, when He wished to take vengeance on them, He commanded him to fight them, to wage war on them, and to be harsh with them. End of the commentary on the sura "By the heaven and the Night-Comer."
